extraction.name: ACL OCL Corpus
extraction.description: ACL OCL is a scholarly corpus derived from the ACL Anthology to assist open scientific research in the Computational Linguistics domain. It integrates and enhances previous versions of the ACL Anthology, contributing metadata, PDF files, citation graphs, and additional structured full texts with sections, figures, and links to a large knowledge resource (Semantic Scholar). The ACL OCL spans seven decades, containing 73K papers alongside 210K figures.
extraction.creator: Shaurya Rohatgi, Yanxia Qin, Benjamin Aw, Niranjana Unnithan, Min-Yen Kan
extraction.publisher: Pennsylvania State University; National University of Singapore
extraction.citeAs: Rohatgi, S., Qin, Y., Aw, B., Unnithan, N., & Kan, M.-Y. (2023). The ACL OCL Corpus: Advancing Open Science in Computational Linguistics. arXiv:2305.14996v2.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: PDF files and metadata were crawled from the ACL Anthology website. Meta information was included from the website as it is more accurate than that obtained by PDF extraction, given its author-driven nature. PDF files longer than 50 pages (mostly conference volume introductions or handbooks) were removed. The dataset undergoes annual updates, during which newly added papers are downloaded and processed by monitoring changes in URLs. Additional information was fetched using Semantic Scholar's API.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Web API, Secondary Data analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Full-text extraction failures occur mostly for papers between the years 2000 to 2015. Only 16.8% of OCL papers have an arxiv_paper_id. Missing sections (19 sections not detected from 21 scientific papers), missing footnotes (25 out of 92), missing figures (28.78%, 19/66), and missing or incorrect tables (31.58% not detected, 46.06% detected with wrong contents or titles) were observed in quality assessment.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: PDF files and metadata from the ACL Anthology website (https://aclanthology.org/), covering 73,285 conference, journal, and workshop papers in the CL domain published from 1952 to September 2022. Additional data linked from the Semantic Scholar Academic Graph (S2AG) via its Graph API.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: PDF files longer than 50 pages were removed. Full texts were extracted from PDFs using GROBID and stored in S2ORC-JSON format. Figures and tables were extracted using PDFFigures 2.0. Language detection was performed using a public language detection toolkit (langdetect by Shuyo, 2010) with title and abstract as inputs. Model-predicted silver topic labels were generated using a PLM-based supervised classifier (SPECTER) trained on 2,545 labeled papers. The dataset is provided in both CSV and Apache Parquet formats.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: PDF files longer than 50 pages were filtered out. Full-text extraction was performed using GROBID, with the S2ORC-JSON format adopted for the full-text schema. Figures and tables were extracted using PDFFigures 2.0. Metadata from the ACL Anthology website was used in preference to PDF-extracted metadata due to higher accuracy. Language detection was applied to each paper using title and abstract. OCL papers were linked to S2AG using the Graph API via ACL Anthology ID.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Topic labels were crawled from the websites of several online-held CL conferences (ACL 2020, EMNLP 2020, ACL-IJCNLP 2021, EACL 2021, NAACL 2021) between 2020 and 2022, yielding 2,545 documents with ground-truth topic labels across 21 topics. These labels were used to train a PLM-based supervised topic classifier (SPECTER), whose predictions were used as silver topic labels for the full OCL corpus. A taxonomy of 21 objective topics was constructed by surveying call-for-papers from major CL conferences (ACL, EMNLP, COLING) from 2000 to 2022.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The PLM-based supervised method (SPECTER) achieved 69% accuracy on the STop test set. A case study on the top 15 cited papers showed 87% accuracy (13/15 correct), higher than the expected 69%, partly due to bias in the distribution of top-cited papers towards dominant topics. Two papers (BLEU and ROUGE) were incorrectly predicted due to insufficient training samples and high overlap with other topics. Silver labels are noted as model-predicted and not gold-standard annotations.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GROBID (full-text extraction from PDFs), PDFFigures 2.0 (figure and table extraction), langdetect/language-detection library for Java (Shuyo, 2010) for language detection, BART-large-MNLI (zero-shot and semi-supervised topic classification), SciBERT and SPECTER (PLM-based supervised topic classification), Yake! and TF-IDF (keyword extraction)
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset undergoes annual updates, during which papers recently added to the ACL Anthology are downloaded and processed. New additions are identified by monitoring changes in URLs. Future plans include providing full-text extraction and information extraction APIs to ACL Anthology and ultimately hosting the OCL data on ACL Anthology itself.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Author names and affiliations are included in the metadata. The dataset contains publication metadata including author lists.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The ACL OCL corpus advances open scientific research in computational linguistics by providing accessible and standardized data resources, promoting reproducibility, and enabling analysis of research trends including the emergence of topics like 'Ethics of NLP'. The corpus highlights underrepresentation of low-resource languages in the CL domain.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The corpus is limited to peer-reviewed, open-access CL papers from the ACL Anthology and does not include other sources. English is the dominant language, and prior research has found that numerous languages remain underrepresented in the ACL Anthology. The distribution of top-cited papers is biased towards dominant topics (e.g., Machine Translation), which affects topic classification accuracy. Silver topic labels generated by the model may contain errors, especially for underrepresented topics.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: OCL is a small-scale collection focused only on peer-reviewed, open-access CL papers from the ACL Anthology and is not a comprehensive corpus like S2ORC. Full-text extraction quality is limited by GROBID's constraints, especially for formatting information such as figures, tables, and in-line equations. Only open-source PDF2text toolkits were used due to budget constraints. The corpus lacks human annotations for specific tasks. Full-text extraction failures are most common for papers from 2000 to 2015. The corpus does not include arXiv CL papers.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, and Validation for NLP tasks including topic classification, document-level information extraction, related work generation, figure caption generation, summarization, coreference resolution, terminology detection, citation network analysis, knowledge graph construction, temporal topic trend analysis, historical language change analysis, and pre-training or fine-tuning scientific language models.
